name: mysti
description: Multi-agent AI coding assistant. Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, and GitHub Copilot brainstorm together, debate approaches, and deliver superior solutions. Like Cursor & Copilot, but with collaborative AI agents.

commands.title: Mysti: Quarantine All User Agent Artifacts (kill switch)

enumDescriptions: Claude Code CLI (Anthropic) - Deep reasoning, complex refactoring, thorough analysis
OpenAI Codex CLI - Quick iterations, familiar GPT style, rapid prototyping
Google Gemini CLI - Fast responses, Google ecosystem integration
Cline - Autonomous coding agent with browser use, file editing, and command execution
GitHub Copilot CLI - GitHub-native AI assistant with seamless GitHub integration
Cursor - AI-powered coding with fast editing and multi-file changes
OpenClaw - Open-source personal AI assistant with multi-model support and Gateway streaming
OpenCode - Multi-provider AI coding agent with support for OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq, and OpenRouter
Ollama - Local LLM inference server supporting Llama, CodeLlama, Mistral, and more
LocalAI - Self-hosted OpenAI-compatible local inference with GPU/CPU support
Qwen Code - Alibaba's AI coding agent with Qwen3-Coder models and multi-provider support
Hermes - NousResearch's self-improving agent with skills, memory, and 300+ models via Nous Portal, OpenRouter, or custom endpoints
Continue - continuedev's open-source coding agent (cn CLI) with hub assistants, rules, and any-model configs
OpenRouter - Unified API gateway routing to 300+ models across providers (free by default, OpenAI-compatible)
Kimi Code - Moonshot AI's terminal coding agent (kimi CLI) with Kimi K2.7 Code / K3 models over the Agent Client Protocol

enumDescriptions: Default — gate changes when access level is Ask permission
Ask before edit — confirm every change
Edit automatically — apply file edits; still ask for commands and deletes
Quick plan — investigate read-only and propose a short plan
Detailed plan — investigate read-only and propose a full plan
mysti.defaultMode.description: Default operation mode. Must match the OperationMode union in src/types.ts — a value offered here that the code does not handle would fall through the permission gate (Plan 23 B1).

mysti.defaultThinkingLevel.description: Default thinking level for AI responses

enumDescriptions: Low — fastest, least reasoning
Medium — balanced
High — thorough reasoning (default)
Extra high — deeper reasoning (newest models)
Max — maximum reasoning effort
mysti.defaultEffortLevel.description: Reasoning effort tier (Claude Code parity). Each backend maps this to its native reasoning control (Claude Code → --effort, Codex → model_reasoning_effort, OpenRouter → reasoning.effort, …). Backends with no reasoning control ignore it. Distinct from thinking level.

mysti.claudeCodeModel.description: Custom model for Claude Code. Overrides the dropdown selection. Leave empty to use the selected model. Example: claude-opus-4-8 (or claude-opus-4-8[1m] for the 1M-context variant)

mysti.claude.backgroundWaitCeilingMs.markdownDescription: How long (ms) the headless Claude Code process waits for **background subagents/workflows** to finish before exiting, so their results are reported back through the turn (sets `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS`; requires `claude` ≥ v2.1.182). Default `600000` (10 min). `0` = wait indefinitely. Raise it if you run long background workflows. If a workflow launched via Claude Code never reports its result, first check `claude --version` is ≥ 2.1.182.

mysti.codexModel.description: Custom model for OpenAI Codex. Overrides the dropdown selection. Leave empty to use the selected model. Example: gpt-5.4-codex

mysti.codexProfile.description: Codex profile from ~/.codex/config.toml. Leave empty to use default profile.

mysti.geminiModel.description: Custom model for Google Gemini. Overrides the dropdown selection. Leave empty to use the selected model. Example: gemini-3-pro-preview

mysti.clineModel.description: Custom model for Cline. Overrides the dropdown selection. Leave empty to use the selected model. Example: claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929

mysti.copilotModel.description: Custom model for GitHub Copilot. Overrides the dropdown selection. Leave empty to use the selected model. Example: claude-opus-4.5

mysti.cursorModel.description: Custom model for Cursor. Overrides the dropdown selection. Leave empty to use the default model. Example: claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929

mysti.openclawModel.description: Custom model for OpenClaw. Overrides the dropdown selection. Leave empty to use the selected model. Example: claude-opus-4-6

mysti.opencodeModel.description: Custom model for OpenCode. Overrides the dropdown selection. Leave empty to use the default model. Example: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5

mysti.qwenCodeModel.description: Custom model for Qwen Code. Overrides the dropdown selection. Leave empty to use the default model. Example: qwen3-coder-plus

mysti.hermesModel.description: Reserved for Hermes model overrides. Hermes selects its model from its own config (`hermes model` / `hermes setup`); this setting currently has no effect on the ACP transport.

mysti.continueModel.description: Custom model for Continue, passed as `cn --model <slug>`. Hub slug in owner/package format (e.g. anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5). Leave empty to use the models in ~/.continue/config.yaml.

mysti.openrouterModel.markdownDescription: Model for the OpenRouter backend, e.g. `openai/gpt-oss-120b:free`, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5`, or `openrouter/free` (free auto-router). Append `:free` for a free variant. Leave empty to use the default (`openrouter/free`). Uses the same key as `mysti.openrouter.apiKey`.

mysti.kimiCodeModel.description: Custom model for Kimi Code (e.g. kimi-for-coding, kimi-for-coding-highspeed, k3, kimi-k2.7-code). Passed to the CLI via the ANTHROPIC_MODEL env; the model is otherwise chosen inside Kimi with `/model`. Leave empty to use the account default.

mysti.customModels.markdownDescription: User-defined custom models per provider, keyed by provider id (e.g. `{ "claude-code": ["claude-opus-4-6[1m]"] }`). These appear in the model dropdown alongside the built-in list and survive marketplace updates. Managed automatically by the "Custom..." model entry in the chat UI.

mysti.codeLens.enabled.description: Show 'Mysti: Explain | Refactor | Write Tests' CodeLens above functions in the editor.

enumDescriptions: AI can only read files, never modify - safest option for exploring codebases
AI asks before each file change - balanced control and productivity
AI can edit files autonomously - maximum speed for trusted tasks
mysti.accessLevel.description: Control what the AI can do with your files. Choose based on your trust level and task requirements.

mysti.autoContext.description: Automatically include open files and selections as context for better AI responses

mysti.planDetection.enabled.description: Detect and show implementation plan options in AI responses. Disable to reduce post-response latency.

mysti.checkpoints.enabled.description: Snapshot the workspace before each chat turn so you can rewind code to any prior turn. Uses a private git repository stored outside your project — it never touches your own .git.

mysti.checkpoints.maxFiles.description: Skip checkpointing when the workspace has more than this many tracked/untracked files (0 = no limit). Protects very large repositories from slow snapshots.

mysti.checkpoints.maxSnapshots.description: Maximum checkpoints to retain per workspace before the oldest are pruned (0 = unlimited).

mysti.compaction.enabled.description: Enable automatic context compaction when token usage exceeds the threshold

mysti.compaction.threshold.description: Context usage percentage at which automatic compaction triggers (50-95%)

mysti.compaction.smart.enabled.markdownDescription: Enable **smart compaction** (requires a connected DeepMyst account). Adds cache-aware timing, a cheap incremental compactor agent, an economic compact-vs-cache decision with a quality floor, cherry-pick retrieval over full history, and an always-on savings display. When off — or when no DeepMyst account is connected — Mysti uses the standard threshold compaction configured above.

mysti.compaction.smart.cheapModel.markdownDescription: Model used by the smart compactor agent for summarization + retrieval scoring, routed through the DeepMyst gateway. A cheap, reliable model is recommended (default `claude-haiku-4-5`).

mysti.compaction.smart.minSummaryTokens.markdownDescription: Quality floor for smart compaction — the compacted prefix is never targeted below this size. Keeps it above the model's minimum cacheable prefix (≈4096 on Opus/Haiku) so the summary still caches, and preserves enough context for quality.

mysti.compaction.smart.retrieval.enabled.markdownDescription: When smart compaction is active, allow parallel cherry-pick retrieval over the full on-disk history to pull back relevant summarized-away context. Only fires when a prompt needs buried history (gated by a free local relevance check), so it rarely adds cost.

mysti.deepmyst.gatewayUrl.markdownDescription: Base URL of the DeepMyst OpenAI-compatible LLM **gateway** used by smart compaction (`/v1/chat/completions`). Distinct from `mysti.deepmyst.apiUrl` (the MCP/REST host). The same `dm_` key authenticates both. Machine-scoped so a workspace can't redirect your key; the client also only ever sends it to a `*.deepmyst.com` host.

mysti.models.autoRefresh.description: Automatically refresh provider model lists in the background a few seconds after startup (live discovery via CLI/HTTP where supported). Disable to rely only on the bundled/curated and cached lists.

mysti.mysti.coordinatorModel.markdownDescription: **Pin** the **Mysti agent**'s coordinator to a single model, routed through the **DeepMyst gateway** using your signed-in DeepMyst account (no local key needed; a free account works). Leave **empty** (default) to rotate the curated free-model list in `mysti.mysti.freeModels` — on a rate-limit Mysti rolls over to the next free model, then to the paid `mysti.mysti.fallbackModel`. Set an id (e.g. `openrouter/openai/gpt-oss-120b:free` — the `openrouter/` prefix picks the OpenRouter provider via the gateway, or a bare gateway model like `claude-haiku-4-5`) to disable rotation. (Only used when no `mysti.openrouter.apiKey` is set — an OpenRouter key opts into OpenRouter directly instead.)

mysti.mysti.freeModels.markdownDescription: Ordered list of **free** models (routed through the DeepMyst gateway) the Mysti coordinator tries when `mysti.mysti.coordinatorModel` is empty. Defaults to STRONG concrete free models (strongest first, from https://openrouter.ai/collections/free-models) rather than OpenRouter's random `openrouter/free` auto-router — the coordinator has to follow the delegation protocol reliably, and the random router can pick weak models that can't. On any transient failure — rate-limit, provider drop, 5xx, mid-stream fallback — Mysti advances to the next entry (graceful degradation), and only after all are exhausted falls back to the paid `mysti.mysti.fallbackModel`. To use the random free auto-router instead, set this to `["openrouter/openrouter/free"]` (note the doubled prefix: `openrouter/` selects the OpenRouter provider via litellm, `openrouter/free` is the router slug; a bare `openrouter/free` mis-parses to a 502). Reorder or trim to taste. Ignored when a single model is pinned in `mysti.mysti.coordinatorModel`.

mysti.mysti.maxDelegations.markdownDescription: Max sub-agent **delegations** per Mysti-agent run (doubled at high effort). The coordinator's own read-only tools (read/ls/grep/diag) have a separate budget and never consume delegation slots. Machine-scoped so a workspace cannot raise your per-run spend ceiling (consistent with the coordinator-model settings).

mysti.mysti.maxTurns.markdownDescription: Hard cap on coordinator **model streams** per Mysti-agent run (doubled at high effort) — the run's spend ceiling. One stream = one turn; a delegation result, a local read-tool result, and a length-continue each start a new turn. Machine-scoped so a workspace cannot raise your per-run spend ceiling. Lower it to cap spend more tightly.

mysti.mysti.memory.markdownDescription: **Unified cross-backend memory** for the Mysti agent: durable project facts (learned by the coordinator via a `remember` tool) are stored per-workspace and injected into every future Mysti run — so the 14 backends behave like one agent that knows your project. Injected as untrusted, nonce-fenced data. Disable to stop persisting/injecting learnings. Review or delete individual facts with the `Mysti: View & Prune Mysti Memory` command.

enumDescriptions: No cross-vendor review.
After a delegation edits files, a DIFFERENT-vendor agent reviews the change read-only and its findings are fed back to the coordinator (advisory — never blocks).
mysti.mysti.crossReview.markdownDescription: **Cross-vendor review** (the coordinator-only superpower): after a delegation modifies files, Mysti dispatches a *different-vendor* backend (e.g. Anthropic wrote it → OpenAI or Google reviews it) in READ-ONLY mode to catch bugs the writer's own model would miss — decorrelated blind spots no single-vendor agent gets. `advisory` runs one review per run and feeds findings back to the coordinator; `off` (default) disables it. Costs one extra read-only delegation; requires ≥2 different-vendor backends installed.

enumDescriptions: Never add a verification step.
After a delegation edits files, run a free diagnostics check and nudge the coordinator to verify (run tests/build) before finishing.
mysti.mysti.verify.markdownDescription: Verification loop for the **Mysti agent**: after a delegation modifies files, Mysti automatically runs a read-only editor-diagnostics check and prompts its coordinator to verify the change (e.g. run the project's tests/build) before answering — the single biggest 'did it actually work' quality lever. `off` disables it.

enumDescriptions: The Mysti agent coordinates and delegates only — it cannot write files or run commands itself (default).
The Mysti agent can create/edit files ITSELF (gated write/edit tools), so it works even with no backend installed.
mysti.mysti.localExecution.markdownDescription: **Standalone execution for the Mysti agent (Plan 19).** When `on`, the `@mysti` coordinator gets its OWN gated `write` / `edit` tools AND a **sandboxed `bash`** tool (run tests/builds/linters) — so it works even with no CLI backend installed. Every op goes through the **same permission gate** as CLI backends (default-deny in ask modes), is **workspace-scoped** (secret files blocked), and is **checkpointed** (undoable); `bash` additionally runs in an **OS sandbox** (macOS Seatbelt / Linux bwrap — no network, writes limited to the workspace; on platforms without a sandbox only genuinely read-only commands run). Destructive commands (`rm`, `sudo`, `git push --force`, `curl|sh`, container/daemon control, …) are hard-blocked; chained/compound commands and anything not on the read-only allowlist ALWAYS require explicit approval (a command auto-runs only when it is read-only-safe, non-compound, sandboxed, and a capable coordinator model is pinned). Machine-scoped on purpose: a workspace cannot enable it. Disabled in untrusted workspaces and in plan / read-only tiers. A pinned capable coordinator model (`mysti.mysti.coordinatorModel`) is recommended.

enumDescriptions: The Mysti agent's sandboxed bash has NO network access (default).
Allow network access inside the Mysti agent's bash sandbox (needed for installs/downloads — increases the prompt-injection surface).
mysti.mysti.bashNetwork.markdownDescription: Whether the `@mysti` agent's sandboxed `bash` tool may access the **network**. Default `off` (the sandbox blocks all egress) — the safest posture, since the coordinator model is prompt-injectable. Turn `on` only if you need the agent to run installs/downloads itself; it widens the attack surface. Requires `mysti.mysti.localExecution` = `on`. Machine-scoped.

enumDescriptions: Off (default) - the coordinator cannot see the agent catalog
Prose - search and read personas/skills/roles
Full - also author and run capabilities (not yet implemented)
mysti.mysti.skills.markdownDescription: **Agent catalog for the Mysti agent (Plan 20).** When set to `prose`, the `@mysti` coordinator can **search and read** the project's reusable working practices - the bundled personas/skills/roles plus any you have written in `.mysti/agents/` - instead of re-deriving the same procedures every session. Retrieval only: it reads files you already have and calls nothing, so there is no permission card. What it reads is injected as **reference material, not instructions**, and only integrity-verified bundled content is ever trusted further (workspace- and user-authored files are fenced). Costs nothing when off, and nothing when fewer than 8 artifacts exist. `full` will additionally allow authoring and running capabilities - **not implemented yet**, and it currently behaves as `prose`. Machine-scoped so a workspace cannot enable it.

enumDescriptions: The Mysti agent cannot call your connected external tools (default).
The Mysti agent can call your CONNECTED external MCP tools (Gmail, Slack, Notion, databases, …) — every call requires explicit approval.
mysti.mysti.mcpTools.markdownDescription: **External MCP tools for the Mysti agent (Plan 19).** When `on`, the `@mysti` coordinator can call the external tools you've **connected via DeepMyst** (Gmail, Slack, Trello, Notion, databases, …), discovered live through the DeepMyst broker. Every call is an un-undoable network side effect (sending mail, creating a ticket), so it **always** requires an explicit approval card — it is never auto-approved, even in full-access or autonomous-aggressive. Only your already-connected tools are callable (a model-invented tool name is refused); results re-enter the model as untrusted, nonce-fenced data. Requires a signed-in DeepMyst account and a trusted workspace. Off by default; machine-scoped so a workspace cannot enable it. Budget: `mysti.mysti.maxMcpCalls` per run.

mysti.mysti.maxMcpCalls.markdownDescription: Max **external MCP tool calls** the `@mysti` agent may make per run (each still requires explicit approval). NOT effort-scaled. Machine-scoped so a workspace cannot raise your per-run external-call ceiling. Requires `mysti.mysti.mcpTools` = `on`.

mysti.mysti.fallbackModel.markdownDescription: Cheap **paid** gateway model the Mysti agent falls back to when **every** free model (`mysti.mysti.freeModels`, or the pinned `mysti.mysti.coordinatorModel`) is rate-limited (free-tier OpenRouter models have a hard requests/min cap). Default `claude-haiku-4-5` — covered by a free DeepMyst account's monthly credit allowance. Set to empty (`""`) for free-only (accept rate-limit errors, never spend credits).

mysti.openrouter.apiKey.markdownDescription: **Optional power-user opt-in.** An OpenRouter API key (`sk-or-...`) to run the **Mysti agent**'s coordinator on OpenRouter **free** models INSTEAD of the DeepMyst gateway. Leave empty (default) to run through your DeepMyst account. Get one at https://openrouter.ai/keys. Machine-scoped so a workspace can't read or redirect it; only ever sent to `openrouter.ai`. The `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` environment variable is used as a fallback.

mysti.openrouter.coordinatorModel.markdownDescription: Model the Mysti agent uses for its own coordination (decompose/synthesize). `auto` (default) discovers a currently-available OpenRouter **free** model at runtime (the roster rotates, so ids are never hardcoded). Set an explicit id (e.g. `openai/gpt-oss-120b:free`) to pin one, or `openrouter/free` to use OpenRouter's free meta-router.

mysti.deepmyst.apiUrl.markdownDescription: Base URL of the DeepMyst API used for brokered MCP connections (Plan 04). The user's `dm_` API key is sent as `Authorization: Bearer`; DeepMyst exposes MCP tools at `/api/v1/mcp/{agent}`. Machine-scoped so a workspace can't redirect your key; the client also only ever sends it to a `*.deepmyst.com` host.

mysti.deepmyst.webUrl.markdownDescription: Base URL of the DeepMyst web app, opened in the browser for Clerk sign-in/sign-up and for managing connections.

mysti.deepmyst.useInLocalClis.markdownDescription: Expose your DeepMyst MCP connections (Smithery/Composio) to your local AI CLIs (Claude Code, Gemini, Qwen, OpenCode, Codex, Cline) by writing the per-user MCP broker endpoint (`/api/v1/me/mcp`) into each CLI's MCP config, with your `dm_` key as the Bearer. **Off by default** — when on, your `dm_` key is written into those config files (including the workspace `.mcp.json`, which may be committed to git). Toggle it from the DeepMyst Connections panel.

mysti.agents.maxTokenBudget.description: Limit tokens used for agent context. Set to 0 for unlimited (default). Use lower values to reduce API costs.

mysti.agents.skillSources.description: GitHub repositories to discover skills from (SKILL.md convention). Format: owner/repo, optionally with /path and @branch — e.g. 'garrytan/gstack' or 'anthropics/skills@main'. Used by the 'Mysti: Import Skills from GitHub' command. Application-scoped so workspaces cannot inject sources.

mysti.collab.maxConcurrent.description: Maximum collaborators (advisor/critic/reviewer/coworker) dispatched at once when using @agent:role mentions or the /consult, /review, /critique, /panel commands. Higher values run more agents in parallel but use more resources.

mysti.permission.timeout.description: Seconds to wait for permission approval (0 = no timeout, requires explicit action). Machine-scoped: a workspace cannot shorten it to fast-track an auto-accept.

enumDescriptions: Automatically approve the action when timeout expires
Automatically deny the action when timeout expires
No timeout - require explicit user action
AI makes an intelligent decision using safety classification and learned preferences when timeout expires
mysti.permission.timeoutBehavior.description: Behavior when a permission request times out. Machine-scoped (security): a repository's workspace settings cannot flip this to auto-accept to silently approve delegation/edit writes — the workspace-raises-authority escalation review[0] closed.

mysti.semiAutonomous.timeout.description: Seconds before AI takes over in semi-autonomous mode. Applies to both permission requests and questions.

mysti.useShellForCli.description: Run AI provider CLIs using a shell (sets shell=true when spawning processes). Enable this on Windows if you see "spawn EINVAL" errors with CLI .cmd wrappers.

mysti.debugVerbose.description: Pass --verbose flag to CLI providers (Claude Code, Cline). Adds extra diagnostic output but may slow responses. Only enable for debugging.

mysti.debug.performanceLogging.markdownDescription: Log detailed performance instrumentation to the Debug Console with the `[Mysti][perf]` prefix: activation and provider-init timings, panel time-to-usable, time-to-first-token, per-chunk render cost percentiles, and heap samples. When off, only a few coarse timings (activation, panel ready, first token) are recorded. Only enable when diagnosing performance issues.

enumDescriptions: Only auto-approve read and create operations
Auto-approve edits to existing files within workspace
Auto-approve most operations (destructive actions always blocked)
mysti.autonomous.safetyMode.description: Safety level for autonomous mode decisions

mysti.autonomous.maxSessionDuration.description: Maximum hours for an autonomous session (0 = unlimited)

mysti.autonomous.maxMemoryEntries.description: Maximum number of memory entries to store

mysti.autonomous.blockPatterns.description: Additional regex patterns to block in autonomous mode (e.g. dangerous commands)

mysti.autonomous.allowFileCreation.description: Allow autonomous mode to create new files

mysti.autonomous.allowFileEdit.description: Allow autonomous mode to edit existing files

mysti.autonomous.allowBashCommands.description: Allow autonomous mode to run bash commands (destructive commands always blocked)

enumDescriptions: Provide a high-level goal and the agent continues until it's met
Provide a list of tasks and the agent works through them sequentially
mysti.autonomous.continuationMode.description: How autonomous mode handles task continuation

mysti.commitSignature.enabled.description: Track when Mysti creates git commits for the Trail Blazer badge

mysti.fileDecorations.enabled.description: Show sparkle 'M' badge on files modified by Mysti in the VS Code Explorer

mysti.fileDecorations.duration.description: How long (in hours) to show file decoration badges after a file is modified by Mysti

mysti.projectContext.enabled.description: Read mysti.md and .mysti/rules/ for project-specific instructions (like CLAUDE.md)

mysti.autoMemory.enabled.description: Automatically learn and remember project patterns across sessions (like Claude Code's auto-memory)

mysti.visualTest.enabled.description: Enable visual testing. When off, neither you nor the AI can open a browser from Mysti.

mysti.visualTest.devServerCommand.description: Dev server command (e.g. 'npm run dev'). Auto-detected from your package.json scripts (dev/start/serve) if empty. Starting it always asks for your approval first.

mysti.visualTest.url.description: URL to test after dev server starts

enumDescriptions: Chromium (Chrome/Edge) — fastest and most compatible
Firefox — Gecko engine
WebKit (Safari) — for macOS/iOS testing
mysti.visualTest.browser.description: Browser engine for screenshots and interactions

mysti.visualTest.headless.description: Run browser in headless mode (no visible window)

mysti.visualTest.interactionsEnabled.description: Allow AI to interact with the page (click, type, navigate, scroll)

mysti.visualTest.serverReadyPattern.description: Regex pattern to detect when the dev server is ready (matched against stdout). Machine-scoped and length-capped so a cloned repo cannot inject a catastrophically-backtracking pattern.

mysti.visualTest.allowedOrigins.description: Origins the visual-testing browser may reach. Loopback-only by default: a browser that can fetch arbitrary URLs and screenshot them back to a model is an exfiltration channel. An entry without a port allows any port on that host. Cloud metadata addresses are blocked even if listed.

mysti.visualTest.allowModelDevServerComm.description: Allow the AI to supply the dev-server shell command. Off by default — the command comes from mysti.visualTest.devServerCommand or your package.json, so a prompt-injected model has no command to name. Turning this on re-introduces a model-to-shell path, gated by a modal confirmation.

enumDescriptions: The AI can look at the page but not touch it
The AI may click, type, hover, select, scroll and navigate within your app — each batch needs your approval
mysti.visualTest.agentInteractions.description: How much the AI may interact with your running app during a visual look.

mysti.visualTest.interactions.description: How much the Visual Test dashboard (your own clicks) may interact with the page.

enumDescriptions: The Mysti agent cannot open a browser
The Mysti agent can render your app and look at it (look/act)
mysti.mysti.visualTools.description: Let the Mysti agent SEE your running app: render it in a real browser and read back console errors, failed requests, layout/contrast problems, the accessibility tree and a screenshot. Requires a trusted workspace and Playwright browsers (npx playwright install chromium). Off by default — it starts a dev server and a browser.

mysti.mysti.maxVisualLooks.description: Maximum times the Mysti agent may look at the running app in a single run (doubled on high effort).

enumDescriptions: OpenAI GPT Image 1.5 — best quality, fastest
OpenAI GPT Image 1 — great quality
OpenAI GPT Image 1 Mini — budget-friendly
Google Gemini 3.1 Flash — fast, free tier
Google Gemini 3 Pro — highest quality
Disabled
mysti.canvas.imageGenerationProvider.description: Image generation provider for Canvas reimagination and draft features

enumDescriptions: OpenAI Sora 2 — high quality video generation
Google Veo 3.1 — Google's video generation model
Disabled
mysti.canvas.videoGenerationProvider.description: Video generation provider for Canvas /video command

mysti.canvas.openaiApiKey.description: OpenAI API key for GPT Image and Sora video generation
mysti.canvas.openaiApiKey.markdownDeprecationMessage: **Deprecated.** Canvas API keys are now stored securely in VSCode SecretStorage instead of settings. Any value here is migrated automatically on first activation and then cleared. Enter or change the key from the Canvas config panel.

mysti.canvas.geminiApiKey.description: Google Gemini API key for image and Veo video generation
mysti.canvas.geminiApiKey.markdownDeprecationMessage: **Deprecated.** Canvas API keys are now stored securely in VSCode SecretStorage instead of settings. Any value here is migrated automatically on first activation and then cleared. Enter or change the key from the Canvas config panel.

mysti.canvas.defaultVariantCount.description: Number of variants to generate for reimagination

mysti.canvas.stitchApiKey.description: Google Stitch API key for UI screen generation (get from stitch.withgoogle.com → Settings → API Keys)
mysti.canvas.stitchApiKey.markdownDeprecationMessage: **Deprecated.** The Stitch API key is now stored securely in VSCode SecretStorage instead of settings. Any value here is migrated automatically on first activation and then cleared. You will be prompted to enter the key when a Stitch command runs.

mysti.canvas.stitchDeviceType.description: Default device type for Stitch screen generation

mysti.canvas.stitchModel.description: Stitch model: GEMINI_3_PRO (higher quality) or GEMINI_3_FLASH (faster)

mysti.canvas.stitchVariantCount.description: Number of design variants to generate with Stitch

mysti.canvas.stitchCreativeRange.description: Creative range for Stitch variants: REFINE (conservative), EXPLORE (balanced), REIMAGINE (radical)

colors.description: Color for the Mysti file decoration badge in the Explorer

walkthroughs.title: Get Started with Mysti
walkthroughs.description: Set up your multi-agent AI coding assistant in 2 minutes

steps.title: Open the Mysti Panel
steps.description:
Click the Mysti icon in the Activity Bar or press ``Cmd+Shift+M`` (``Ctrl+Shift+M`` on Windows/Linux) to open the chat panel.

[Open Mysti](command:mysti.openChat)

media.altText: Mysti chat panel with welcome screen

steps.title: Set Up an AI Provider
steps.description:
Install and authenticate at least one AI CLI tool. Claude Code is recommended for the best experience.

[Open Settings](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22mysti.defaultProvider%22%5D)

media.altText: Mysti settings panel showing provider options

steps.title: Send Your First Message
steps.description:
Ask Mysti to explain code, fix a bug, write tests, or generate new features. You're Mysting now!

[Open Chat](command:mysti.openChat)

steps.title: Try Multi-Agent Brainstorm
steps.description:
Enable Brainstorm Mode to have two AI agents collaborate, debate, and synthesize solutions together. Pick any 2 of 15 providers.

[Open Settings](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22mysti.brainstorm.enabled%22%5D)

media.altText: Brainstorm mode with two AI agents collaborating

steps.title: Star Mysti on GitHub
steps.description:
If Mysti is useful, [star it on GitHub](https://github.com/DeepMyst/Mysti) to help other developers discover it!

Join the community and help shape the future of multi-agent AI coding.
